item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Serbia’s President Vučić resigns: a one-man show

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-10-02

On 27 September, Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić resigned from office eight months before the conclusion of his second and constitutionally final term. Until a successor is elected, his responsibilities as head of state will be undertaken by parliamentary speaker Ana Brnabić, a long-standing close associate. Brnabić is also responsible for setting the date of the presidential election, which must be held within 90 days of the formal submission of Vučić’s resignation to parliament, and thus no later than 27 December, the final Sunday of the year.

Vučić’s resignation is aimed at enabling his return to position of prime minister following the snap parliamentary election scheduled for 25 October. By stepping down as head of state, he also seeks to avoid accusations of leveraging his office for party campaigning, despite having actively campaigned for several months. Additionally, scheduling the presidential election separately, given its tendency to generate high voter turnout, is intended to diminish opposition mobilisation in the parliamentary contest, particularly among the student movement.

item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-10-02

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.
